subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: NebulaCorp amendment — pricing/proration & implementation timeline
messages:
From: Julie Park <julie.park@nebulacorp.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nebulacorp.com
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form — proposed amendment (redlines attached)

Laura —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is NebulaCorp's consolidated redline to the MSA and Order Form focused on the additional reserved capacity and a short SOW tweak (3.2: ingest window). High-level asks:

- Clarify proration treatment for mid-quarter capacity top-ups (we propose prorated credit for unused months).
- Add an implementation milestone tied to the first 30-day performance ramp; we want acceptance criteria.
- Limit the indemnity carve-out for telemetry (we're asking for a narrowly-tailored clause).

We haven't edited pricing lines — we need Redwood to confirm whether the add-on capacity will be billed pro rata or as a new monthly SKU effective the date of activation. Please review with your finance/legal and get back with a suggested approach.

Files: Nebula_Amendment_v3_redline.docx (redline), pricing_workbook note.

Best,
Julie Park
Director, Strategic Sourcing
NebulaCorp





From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Julie Park <julie.park@nebulacorp.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — proposed amendment (redlines attached)

Julie —

Thanks for sending the consolidated redline and the call earlier. We're reviewing with Legal and Finance now. Quick answers up front while we loop them in:

- Billing: our standard approach for top-ups is pro rata for the remainder of the billing month and then the full SKU on the following billing cycle, unless the customer asks for amortization over the remaining term. We can propose a compromise (prorate first month + optional amortization across remaining term).
- Acceptance criteria: agree it's reasonable to add a 30-day ramp milestone with objective tests (latency P95, throughput targets, and KV-cache warmup checks).
- Indemnity carve-outs: we'll need Legal to weigh in — passing to Markus.

I've attached a short note with the two practical billing options we typically present ("Immediate SKU" vs "Amortized Top-up"). Jonas and I will coordinate the implementation milestone language. Expect a draft amendment from us by Monday.

Would you prefer DocuSign for execution?

Warmly,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0142

Attachment: nebula-pricing-workbook-may2028.xlsx (internal pricing scenarios)
From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Nebula redline review — indemnity + acceptance language

Laura / Jonas —

Reviewing Julie's redline. Two points to flag for negotiation:

1) Indemnity: Nebula's proposed carve-out language is broader than we can accept as-is. Recommendation: narrow the carve-out to telemetry-derived claims where Redwood's data handling complies with the written deployment spec and documented integrations. Add a "material breach" threshold and an obligation for Nebula to mitigate.

Proposed edit (short): replace their paragraph with "Telemetry-related claims shall be subject to Section X.Y where Redwood's processing is consistent with the agreed deployment spec; absent material deviation by Redwood, Nebula's indemnity obligations remain in full." (I'll put exact wording in the redline).

2) Acceptance criteria / milestone: their ask for specific latency percentiles is acceptable, but we need to attach an operational test plan as an Exhibit (so both sides agree on measurement windows and tooling). Suggest we: (a) accept a 30-day ramp with objective KPIs; (b) require sign-off from a named Nebula engineering rep and Redwood's onboarding lead; (c) include an automatic remediation window (15 days) before credits are applied.

3) Billing/proration: Finance prefers the "prorate first month, then full SKU" flow. If Nebula wants amortization we can offer it as a paid option with a small admin fee; else, offer a credit if termination occurs within X months.

I'll produce a redline with these adjustments and a short comment box describing tradeoffs. If you want, I can also include a two-line clause that restricts telemetry carve-outs to data that was neither altered nor requested outside the agreed scope.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Contracts
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachment: internal_markus_redline_notes.txt (legal notes)
From: Julie Park <julie.park@nebulacorp.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nebulacorp.com
Date: Fri, 12 May 2028 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — proposed amendment (redlines attached)

Laura / Markus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifying points from our side after internal review:

- Nebula prefers amortization (spread the activation charge over the remaining term) for budgeting reasons. If an admin fee is required, we need to understand magnitude — can Redwood share the typical admin fee percentage?
- For acceptance, we can sign off on an Exhibit test plan; we'll propose a Nebula engineering contact if you draft the template.
- On indemnity: we can live with a more narrowly-crafted carve-out as long as it doesn't broaden to cover negligent acts by Nebula employees.

We can be flexible on the remediation window; 15 days seems okay. Do you have sample amortization schedules we can review?

Julie

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Julie Park <julie.park@nebulacorp.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 May 2028 10:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — proposed amendment (redlines attached)

Julie —

Attached is Redwood's draft amendment ("Nebula_Amendment_v3_redline.docx") and a short amortization schedule example. Key points:

- Option A (Standard): prorate first partial month, then monthly SKU going forward. No admin fee.
- Option B (Amortized): charge full activation amount but amortize over remaining term (we suggested 6/9/12 month bands). Admin fee = 2% of the activation charge if amortized longer than 6 months (covers accounting adjustments).
- Acceptance & Exhibit: added an Exhibit A: Operational Acceptance Tests (measurement windows, P95 latency, throughput baseline, KV-cache warmup checks). Requires sign-off from Nebula Eng lead and Redwood Onboarding PM.
- Indemnity: Markus' narrowed carve-out is in the doc; expressly excludes Nebula negligence and requires Nebula mitigation steps.

If these align with you, we'll prepare a clean amendment and a DocuSign packet for execution. If you prefer a different amortization band or admin fee, call me and we can negotiate.

Link for review: https://drive.google.com/nebula/amendment-review (internal link)

Cheers,
Laura

Attachment: Nebula_Amendment_v3_redline.docx, nebula-amortization-example.pdf
From: Julie Park <julie.park@nebulacorp.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nebulacorp.com
Date: Tue, 16 May 2028 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Final - Nebula amendment approach OK (DocuSign next)

Laura / Jonas / Markus —

We're aligned internally. Nebula will take Option B (Amortized) with the 9-month band and accept the 2% admin fee. We also confirm Exhibit A and the acceptance test plan. Please send the DocuSign packet and the final signed-by list (we will sign from Procurement + Engineering director).

Two quick asks before routing: please add a short clause that defines the "remaining term" calculation (calendar months remaining at the date of activation) and confirm whether credits are prorated back if Nebula downgrades before amortization completes.

Please route and we'll turn immediately.

Thanks —
Julie Park
Director, Strategic Sourcing
NebulaCorp
